messages.author: 2f3428d3166aad1c
messages.subject: Interactive table example
parts:
I've seen a few posts showing nice applications of using shiny with various jQuery table plugins.  I thought I'd share a piece of an app I'm working on that illustrates how easy / possible it is to use shiny to do everything - multi-column sort, pagination, filtering, etc.  This is nice in that all the data operations can be handled in R and just what is being viewed is sent to the browser (I suppose it might be possible to get datatables to do such server-side processing with shiny/R).  There is also some d3 goodness for interactive filtering.

The code is quite messy (and probably buggy) and I probably won't release it until everything is working well and it is all cleaned up.  I hope this will serve as an example of the versatility of shiny.

http://glimmer.rstudio.com/rhafen/awesomeTable/

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Interactive table example
parts:
Very impressive work, Ryan!

Haider, d3 is pretty low level, much more so than something like googleVis. I do think we will eventually need to establish best practices for how to integrate d3 into Shiny apps, and no doubt Shiny itself will change to make d3 integration easier, but ultimately it's hard for me to imagine a package that would make d3 generally useful for R users (short of an R-to-JavaScript transpiler... *shudder*...)

However, what seems inevitable is that people will build generally useful d3 components and then create R bindings to them. So instead of the "d3 for R" package you might have "plot-d3"[0] or "gis-d3" or "igraph-d3" packages. And of course we would want to ensure that those components can drop right into Shiny.
